subject: Post-demo compare playbook & lab kickoff — proposed tests and SLA checklist
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam@acme-data.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — benchmark scope/questions

Marissa — thanks again for the demo. A few quick follow-ups from our side so we can scope a fair A/B with our engineering team: 

- Can you confirm the exact p95/p99 latency measurement you run (server-side only, network included?). We need apples-to-apples with our hyperscaler endpoints.
- We're most concerned about microburst spikes for short inputs (<=64 tokens) and sustained throughput for longer document batches (tokens/sec). Our preliminary target: p95 < 120ms and sustained 18k tokens/sec for our 4096-window workloads. Can Redwood meet that with your recommended model/config?
- For the A/B we want: Redwood hosted endpoint vs our GCP endpoint (same model family/quantization). Can Redwood run the test in our VPC or provide a private endpoint to avoid egress variance?
- Data residency & logs: need to confirm log retention and token-level traces (for debugging) won't be stored beyond 30 days without a separate agreement.

Attaching: short doc with sample traces and our SOC2 questionnaire.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Park
Director, Engineering
Acme Data Labs

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — benchmark scope/questions

Sam — great to connect today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we all have alignment before the lab kickoff: 

Recap of ask:
- Run head-to-head A/B: Redwood hosted endpoint (dedicated instance) vs Acme's GCP endpoint.
- Metrics: p95 and p99 (server processing time), tokens/sec sustained over 10-minute runs, cold-start p95, and microburst (short batch) p95.
- Test inputs: two slices — short (<=64 tokens) and long (average 1024 tokens).
- Acceptance targets (your baseline): p95 < 120ms for short; sustained 18k tokens/sec for long.

Proposed plan (kickoff -> lab -> readout):
1) Lab kickoff meeting (1 hr) — align infra, network, metric definitions, and runbook. (propose Wed 7/3 10am PT)
2) Prepare test harness & configs — we will provide a lightweight runner that emits identical request traces and collects server-side timing.
3) Run three experiments:
   - A: baseline (your GCP) vs Redwood default config
   - B: Redwood with KV cache enabled + batching tuned to your distribution
   - C: Redwood quantized variant (if applicable) to show cost/latency trade-offs
4) Collect p95/p99, tokens/sec, tail-latency histograms, and sample outputs for quality checks.
5) Readout (2 hr) with ops + eng to agree on next steps.

Network / residency note: we can support a Private Endpoint (VPC peering or customer-managed VPC egress) to minimize network variance. We'll include the private-flow diagram in the kickoff packet. Regarding logs: Redwood defaults to 30-day retention for debug traces; we can provide a contract amendment for 30-day retention with restricted access.

Attachments: draft lab scope (acme-lab-scope-v1.pdf) and our preliminary latency matrix template.

Next actions: please confirm kickoff time and include your procurement contact if you want us to start NDA/contract prep.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — benchmark scope/questions

Sam / Marissa — quick technical notes to make the A/B rigorous (so the readout is actionable):

Measurement methodology (server-side p95/p99):
- We'll instrument per-request server-side processing time (token generation only) and also capture total time including ingress/egress to compare network effect. Both numbers will be included but labeled clearly.
- For p95/p99 we will use the 'steady-state' window (exclude warm-up 60s). Cold-starts will be reported separately.

Test harness config suggestions:
- Short-slice test: 10k requests in 10 runs (1k each), input length sampled <=64 tokens, concurrency ramp 1 -> 32.
- Long-slice test: 5 runs of 10 minutes each, average 1024 tokens, concurrency set to hit throughput target or facility limit.
- Microburst: 200 requests at concurrency 128 with short inputs to surface tail behavior.

Compare dimensions:
- Same model family & quantization level; if different quantization is required we'll add a step to report quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE / token-level perplexity where applicable).
- We'll export raw timing CSVs so your SREs can re-calc with their tooling.

Operational constraints:
- If you want VPC-hosted testing, please share an engineer to do peering or provide a temporary private endpoint. We can run from Redwood side if you prefer to avoid peering.

I'll prepare the harness repo and the exact runbook tonight. If you confirm kickoff Wed 7/3 10am PT I'll send the invite and the Repo + runner link.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
